baptisma, baptismatis n.

noun, third declension

Greek βάπτισμα, a dipping; the Church’s word from the Vulgate and the Fathers on (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • baptismus, baptismī m. — baptism

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Mc. 11.30 (Lewis & Short); Cod. Th. 16.6.1 (Lewis & Short)

    A parallel form; Tertullian and the Vulgate also have the neuter baptismum (Lewis & Short).

  • lavācrum, lavācrī n. — the washing of baptism, the font

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Tit. 3.5; M-O s.v. baptism

    Classically a bath; Paul’s lavācrum regenerātiōnis, the washing of new birth; sacrum lavācrum in Morgan–Owens.

Examples

  • Ūnus Dominus, ūna fidēs, ūnum baptisma.

    One Lord, one faith, one baptism.Vulg. Eph. 4.5

  • per lavācrum regenerātiōnis et renovātiōnis Spīritūs Sānctī

    through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy SpiritVulg. Tit. 3.5

See also baptize, godfather, godmother, godchild, Epiphany.

SourcesLewis & Short: baptisma · Lewis & Short: baptismus · Lewis & Short: lavacrum
